territorial_scope.description: Applies to covered entities receiving CHIPS funds, their affiliated group members and related entities, reaching their transactions involving foreign countries of concern.

evidence.quote: the covered entity and members of the affiliated group may not engage in any significant transaction

summary.short: Final NIST rule (15 CFR Part 231) setting conditions on CHIPS Act funding recipients: bars significant semiconductor manufacturing capacity expansions and certain joint research or technology licensing with foreign entities of concern, subject to exceptions; requires notification and records; effective November 24, 2023.
summary.long: Final rule of the National Institute of Standards and Technology implementing CHIPS Act conditions that keep CHIPS Incentives Program funding from benefiting foreign countries of concern. Subpart A defines key terms, including foreign entity of concern, legacy semiconductor and semiconductors critical to national security. Sec. 231.202 bars covered entities and affiliated group members, for 10 years after the award, significant transactions involving material expansion of semiconductor manufacturing capacity in a foreign country of concern, except for existing legacy facilities and legacy capacity that predominately serves that country's market. Sec. 231.203 bars knowingly engaging in joint research or technology licensing with a foreign entity of concern on technologies or products raising national security concerns; ongoing activities may be grandfathered if memorialized in the required agreement. Sec. 231.204 permits additional conditions against circumvention by related entities, and Sec. 231.205 requires record retention. Subpart C requires notification of planned significant transactions, sets review and reconsideration timelines, and allows mitigation agreements. Violations can lead to recovery of the full federal financial assistance as a debt owed to the government. Subpart D covers periodic legacy-semiconductor notices, liability for false information under 18 U.S.C. 1001, and severability. Effective November 24, 2023.

notes: Final rule published in the Federal Register (vol. 88, no. 184, 25 Sept 2023), effective 24 Nov 2023 per the text. The CHIPS Act is not in the document, so statutory links are text-based only. Internal inconsistencies: (1) §231.306 waives recovery 'for violation of § 231.305(d)', while the summary of changes refers to § 231.302; (2) reconsideration of an initial determination under the Technology Clawback is due within 60 days of the request under §231.305(c)(2), but within 45 days of the initial determination under §231.307(e)(2); (3) §231.305(b) cites '§ paragraph (a)'; (4) 'significant transaction' and 'applicable term' are still used although their definitions were removed, and the $100,000 threshold appears only in the preamble; (5) 'covered entity' is used throughout but not defined in §§231.101–231.121; (6) the classification section refers to 'this proposed rule'. Typos include '28-nonometerer' (§231.118(d)). The 88 FR 17439 proposed rule appears only in the preamble. No named firms are listed; covered entities are addressed generically.

enforcement.authority: Secretary of Commerce (CHIPS Program Office, NIST)
enforcement.triggered_by: Any related entity of the covered entity engages in joint research or technology licensing that would violate the Technology Clawback if engaged in by the covered entity, during the award term
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Recovery of up to the full amount of the Federal financial assistance provided to the covered entity, or lesser remedial measures at the Secretary's discretion

evidence.quote: measures that will allow the Secretary to recover up to the full amount of the Federal financial assistance provided to the covered entity

enforcement.authority: Secretary of Commerce (CHIPS Program Office, NIST)
enforcement.triggered_by: Initial determination by the Secretary that § 231.202 or § 231.203 have been violated

evidence.quote: If the Secretary makes an initial determination that § 231.202 or § 231.203 have been violated, the Secretary may suspend Federal financial assistance.

enforcement.triggered_by: Submission of information to the Secretary under 15 U.S.C. 4652 or this part that is false (section heading: Submission of false information); 18 U.S.C. 1001 also applies to certifications under § 231.305(c)(3)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Penalties under 18 U.S.C. 1001, as amended; penalty amount not stated in this text

evidence.quote: Section 1001 of 18 U.S.C., as amended, shall apply to all information provided to the Secretary under 15 U.S.C. 4652 or under the regulations found in this part.
